newsitem.title: USA: Aames says to change prices, shares fall.
newsitem.headline: Aames says to change prices, shares fall.

text.p: Shares of Aames Financial Corp fell after the company posted 55 percent growth in its third quarter earnings but said a plan to review the pricing of its third party originated product could hurt future earnings.
Shares of the mortgage broker were shorn nearly 23 percent on the New York Stock Exchange on Thursday, falling 3-1/2 to 11-7/8, a new low for the year.
The stock is sharply off from its most recent high in March, when its was trading at more than $32 a share.

In an announcement released on after the market close Wednesday with its third quarter earnings, Aames said it is reviewing the pricing levels in response to changes in the sub-prime mortgage market and "general uncertainties in the capital markets (where) the company has historically funded its negative cash flow".
It said the although the change could hurt earnings, "it will strengthen the company in the long run by improving the company's cash flow and overall financial position".
Aames said earnings per share for the three months ended March 31, 1997 jumped to $0.51 compared to $0.33 last year on a fully diluted basis with 34 percent more weighted shares outstanding.

Net income rose to $17.6 million, from $8.6 million in last year's third quarter and revenues reached $84.1 million, more than double the revenue in the third fiscal quarter last year of $40.6 million.
